subject: EastUS partial throttle & routing decision — customer escalations
messages:
From: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@finovate.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@orbitai.com, support@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-30 08:12 -0700
Subject: High error rate / timeouts from EastUS since 07:40

Jonas —

We started seeing elevated 5xx rates and long tail latencies for inference requests routed to EastUS at ~07:40 PT. Bulk of customer traffic is stable, but our ML callers see a spike in timeouts and some token-generation stalls. This is affecting our streaming clients and is triggering automated retries which compounds load.

Example: 4% 5xx and p99 latency moved from ~210ms to 2.4s across short bursts. We've scoped to your EastUS region; CRM shows many users hitting your hosted endpoints there.

Can you confirm if there's ongoing maintenance or a routing change? We need ETA and a mitigation plan — our product folks are asking if you can fail traffic to WestUS or apply a soft throttle so we don't get repeated retries.

Attaching metric dump from our side (small sample).

Thanks,
Alex Barnes
Platform SRE, Finovate
(attachment: finovate_request_log_excerpt.txt)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@finovate.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Support <support@redwood.com>, PD oncall <pd-oncall@cloudprovider.com>
Date: 2026-05-30 08:28 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate / timeouts from EastUS since 07:40

Alex — I see the spike. We're getting customer reports for OrbitAI as well. I'm escalating to infra and cc'ing Sean and our cloud PD.

Immediate actions: 
- We've opened PD-4512 and our oncall is running live diagnostics.
- I'm preparing a temporary routing change to divert non-critical hostnames off EastUS if we confirm persistent backend throttling.
- Can you paste a representative example request id (X-Request-ID) that hit the error so I can map logs?

I'll follow up in 10 min with more context.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-30 08:36 -07:00
Subject: RE: EastUS partial throttle & routing decision — customer escalations

Team —

Oncall report: several inference workers in az-east-2 are hitting kernel-level GPU preemption and transient NVLink errors, causing retries at the runtime layer. This increases KV cache misses and forces re-computation which spikes p99. Cloud provider shows networking flaps affecting a subset of racks in the EastUS cluster.

Current mitigation options considered:
1) Global route shift: failover a percentage (25–50%) of production traffic for non-SLA-critical routes to WestUS. This is lowest risk for customer experience but must be done carefully to avoid cold-start pressure.
2) Throttle and degrade: apply conservative token caps and reduce streaming chunk sizes for high-throughput customers to limit backend concurrency.
3) Hardware remap: evict affected instances and drain to healthy racks — longer (~30–45m) but permanent.

We need exec sign-off for option 1 during the next 15–20m if we want to avoid more customer escalations.

Eve
Evelyn Hart
SRE Manager — Serving Runtime
(attachment: eastus_metrics_20260530.csv)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-30 08:42 -07:00
Subject: RE: EastUS partial throttle & routing decision — customer escalations

Eve — lean toward option 1 for affected non-critical hostnames and option 3 for the long-term (evict bad racks). For customers on Dedicated capacity (and those with pinned capacity in EastUS) we must not silently failover without notice — coordinate with commercial + support on each.

Action items:
- Jonas: flag impacted customers (OrbitAI, Finovate) and confirm SLA profile (Dedicated? Pinned?).
- Lauren: stand up comms for partners + runbook link.
- Markus: prepare routing policy (weight 0.3 WestUS for hostnames *.preview.redwood.com) and ensure the cold-start budget (warmup pools) is available.

I'll loop in exec if we need an exception for low-latency SLA customers.

—Sean
Chief Revenue Officer
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Support <support@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@finovate.com>, ops@orbitai.com
Date: 2026-05-30 09:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: EastUS partial throttle & routing decision — customer escalations

Quick update and customer notes: 
- OrbitAI: Hosted account, not pinned, high throughput streaming. They want traffic maintained but are seeing retries. Recommend immediate route shift for their control-plane hostnames.
- Finovate: Multi-tenant hosted; tolerate regional failover, but ask to keep them informed.

I authorize routing weight shift for non-Dedicated hostnames to WestUS at 30% immediately. Lauren — please send the comms template and include expected timeline (start, evaluation at 30m, full rollback plan).

Alex / OrbitAI — we will start shifting now. Expect short-lived cold-start latency on some requests; we will monitor and revert if we see regressions. Please share any high-priority request ids and I will route-trace them.

(attachment: runbook_failover_v2.pdf)

—Jonas
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@finovate.com>, ops@orbitai.com, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Support <support@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-01 17:04 -07:00
Subject: Post-action summary: EastUS routing shift and next steps

Alex / OrbitAI — follow-up from our routing action 2026-05-30: we shifted ~30% of non-Dedicated traffic from EastUS to WestUS and monitored for 72 hours. Summary:

- Immediate impact: p99 latency for affected preview hostnames returned to pre-incident ranges within 12 minutes of the shift.
- Errors: 5xx rate for those hostnames dropped from 3.9% to 0.4% in the first 30 minutes.
- Cold starts: ~0.9% of requests experienced single-request latency spikes up to 1.6s during warmup — mitigated by increasing warm pool size for WestUS.

Longer-term actions agreed:
- Infra will evict and reprovision the affected racks in EastUS (INF-2781).
- Product + Optimize will evaluate KV cache prewarming strategies for failovers.
- Commercial to coordinate customer notifications for Dedicated/pinned accounts before any forced failovers.

Attachments included: support_log_snippets.txt (selected traces), eastus_metrics_20260530.csv, runbook_failover_v2.pdf

If you want a 30-minute postmortem call, we'll set it up — otherwise, we'll publish an internal incident review next week and share a customer-facing note.

Thanks for patience and quick coordination.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
